name: Initiation (dīkṣā)
method_summary: The guru, after preliminary purifications and worship of the deity on a maṇḍala and in the fire, performs on the disciple a rite that acts on the soul (not caste or body): in the Śaiva form it binds the disciple to the observances (samaya-dīkṣā) and, in the liberating initiation (nirvāṇa-dīkṣā), purifies the six paths and destroys the bonds through mantra-power; consecrations of sādhaka and ācārya may follow. Pāñcarātra initiation admits to Bhagavān's mantras and worship.
prerequisites: the descent of power (śaktipāta), shown by devotion (Kiraṇa 5); a qualified guru

warnings.text: For the capable the observances remain binding; knowingly breaking them is a great fault.

name: Liberating initiation (nirvāṇa-dīkṣā)
method_summary: The guru ritually traverses and purifies the six paths of the disciple's bondage, burning accumulated and future karma, leaving only the karma that sustains the present body; the disciple becomes a putraka assured of liberation at death. Summary only.

name: Initiation into the observances (samaya-dīkṣā)
method_summary: First Śaiva initiation making the disciple a samayin, bound by post-initiatory rules and entitled to worship and study; for the incapable, the observances may be purified away (seedless initiation).

name: Consecration of teacher and adept (ācāryābhiṣeka, sādhakābhiṣeka)
method_summary: Consecration by bathing with consecrated pots that confers the office of teacher (entitled to initiate and install) or of adept (entitled to master a mantra for powers).

name: Daily worship (pūjā)
method_summary: After bathing and the purifications of self, place, substances, mantras and support, the worshipper purifies the elements of the body, installs mantras on the body (nyāsa), worships the deity inwardly and then outwardly in liṅga, image, maṇḍala or fire with offerings (water, flowers, incense, lamp, food), recitation and praise, and concludes with fire offering and dismissal. Śaiva texts distinguish worship for oneself and for others; the Pāñcarātrin performs it as the third of five daily periods; Vaikhānasas worship the movable image fully and the fixed image with flowers; in Kerala the śānti performs a fixed sequence of daily pūjās.

name: Temple worship for others (parārtha-pūjā)
method_summary: Public worship in temples with installed liṅgas or images, performed by qualified priests on behalf of the king, the realm and devotees; its rules are the subject of most South Indian Āgama redactions.

name: Purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi)
method_summary: In the preliminaries to worship the practitioner mentally dissolves the elements of the body, from earth upward, into their sources, burns away the impure body, and re-creates a pure divine body with mantras before placing mantras on it. Summary only.

name: Placing mantras on the body (nyāsa)
method_summary: The worshipper touches or visualises parts of the body while installing mantras — letters of the alphabet (mātṛkā), the limb-mantras, the five brahma-mantras or the deity's mantras — making the body a divine mantra-body fit to worship the deity; the same is done on the image.

name: Inner worship (antaryāga)
method_summary: Mental worship of the deity installed in the heart (and elsewhere in the body), with imagined offerings, before or instead of external worship.

name: Fire offering (agnikārya, homa)
method_summary: Offerings into a consecrated fire in a prescribed fire-pit as part of daily, initiatory and occasional rites; for Vaikhānasas, the formless (amūrta) worship of Viṣṇu.

name: Installation and consecration (pratiṣṭhā)
method_summary: The series of rites that establish the deity in a liṅga or image and its temple: preparatory rites on the image, its immersion and rest, installation on the pedestal, infusion of the deity through mantras, and the first worship; to be performed throughout with a single root scripture (Śaiva rule), by the tantri alone (Kerala).

warnings.text: Installation done with a sub-division (upabheda) instead of a root āgama destroys the performer and the patron.

name: Temple-building rites from ploughing to installation (karṣaṇādi)
method_summary: Examination and taking possession of the site, ploughing (karṣaṇa), sprouting seeds, laying out the ground-plan (vāstu-maṇḍala), offerings to the site deities, deposit of the foundation (garbhanyāsa), and rites at each stage of construction up to installation; the Kāmika's Pūrvabhāga devotes many chapters to them.
notes: U58 owns Vāstu/Śilpa; here the ritual frame.

name: Renovation and re-consecration (jīrṇoddhāra)
method_summary: Rites for repairing a temple or replacing a damaged image, moving the deity's presence temporarily into a pot or substitute (bālālaya) and re-installing it.

name: Temple festival (mahotsava)
method_summary: The annual festival begun by hoisting the flag, with daily processions of the festival image, offerings to the attendant beings and a concluding bath (avabhṛtha/ārāṭṭu), conducted by the priest or tantri.

name: Annual pavitra offering (pavitrārohaṇa)
method_summary: In Śrāvaṇa (or Nabhasya) the worshipper offers a consecrated thread-garland (pavitra) to the deity to make good all defects in the year's worship and complete the annual observance.

name: Expiatory rites (prāyaścitta)
method_summary: Rites that make good lapses in worship, breaches of observance and pollutions of the temple, graded by the gravity of the fault.

name: The five daily periods (pañcakāla)
method_summary: The Pāñcarātrin's day is divided into approach (abhigamana: purification and going to the Lord), gathering (upādāna: collecting materials for worship), worship (ijyā), study (svādhyāya) and meditation (yoga).
notes: The five also appear, as the Bhāgavatas' practice, in Śaṅkara's report.

name: The five sacraments (pañcasaṃskāra)
method_summary: Initiation of a Vaiṣṇava by branding with the discus and conch (tāpa), the sectarian mark (puṇḍra), a new name (nāma), the mantra, and instruction in worship (yāga). Summary only.
notes: Vaikhānasas do not take the branding (see cpt:garbha-vaisnava).

name: Surrender with six limbs (śaraṇāgati / nyāsa)
method_summary: The seeker takes refuge in the Lord (or in Śrī) as the sole means, with the resolve to do what pleases him, avoidance of what displeases, faith that he will protect, choosing him as protector, laying down oneself and helplessness; thereafter free of grief and fear, without 'mine' or ego.

equivalents.note: Śrīvaiṣṇava prapatti rests on these texts

name: Yoga of the Mṛgendra (seven auxiliaries)
method_summary: Breath-control (propelling, drawing in, holding), withdrawal of the mind from objects once it tastes a little ease, fixation on a chosen place, meditation as repeated thought on it, examination (ūha) of what is to be rejected and accepted, recitation bringing the object near, and absorption as unbroken flow; practised singly or together, they lead to yoga and its powers.
prerequisites: initiation; one's office as teacher or adept

warnings.text: The text itself calls the office of the initiate very hard to fulfil and requires conquest of the senses first.

notes: Breath-retention is named only; no counts or durations are recorded (restricted content policy).

name: Vaikhānasa image worship (samūrtārcana)
method_summary: Daily worship of Viṣṇu with Vedic mantras: eight services to the fixed image by flowers only, thirty-two services to the movable (kautuka) image, invoking the five forms, with fire offering.

name: Prenatal offering to Viṣṇu (viṣṇubali)
method_summary: A saṃskāra performed during pregnancy (the eighth month) dedicating the unborn child to Viṣṇu, on which the Vaikhānasa claim to be Vaiṣṇavas from the womb rests.

name: The daily round of a Kerala temple
method_summary: From the opening of the sanctum at dawn, a fixed series of pūjās through the day (dawn, morning, mid-morning, noon and night pūjās) and processional offerings (śīveli) around the shrine, performed by the śānti; the tantri intervenes for installations, festivals and purifications.
notes: Names often given: uṣaḥpūjā, etiruttu pūjā, pantīraṭi pūjā, ucca pūjā, attāḻa pūjā (from memory; unverified).

name: Offering to the deity's attendants (śrībhūtabali)
method_summary: Offering of cooked rice on the stones of the deity's attendant beings and guardians placed around the shrine, with the festival image carried in procession.

name: Pot-consecration and bathing (kalaśābhiṣeka)
method_summary: Water is consecrated in arrays of pots in which deities are invoked and then poured over the image, to renew its power or to purify after pollution (e.g. sahasrakalaśa in Kerala).

name: Preparatory mantra practice (puraścaraṇa)
method_summary: Before a mantra is used for rites, the practitioner masters it by a prescribed course of repetition with fire offering and other supplements, under dietary and conduct rules. Summary only.
notes: U31 owns mantra practice; no counts recorded here.

name: Observance of the Vidyāpīṭha adept (vidyāvrata)
method_summary: The Vidyāpīṭha sādhaka, to master a goddess-mantra, lives in Kāpālika style — cremation ground, skull-bowl, offerings to yoginīs — for a fixed period. Recorded as summary only; no procedures.

warnings.text: Lakṣmīdhara (a Samaya critic) condemns the Kāpālika and left-hand tantras as deceiving and far from the Vedic path.

notes: Sexual and impure-substance rites of the Yāmala tantras are not described (restricted).

name: Ritual hand gestures (mudrā) of Āgamic worship
method_summary: Hand gestures shown to the deity at invocation, installation and offering, and in purificatory acts, named and described in the ritual manuals.

name: Funeral rites for Śaiva initiates (antyeṣṭi)
method_summary: Special funeral rites for initiates in which the guru ritually completes the soul's release; described in the Siddhānta paddhatis.
